absent: Architectural predicates for huge leaf support and subordinate page release behavior are not shown.
Translation buffer flush and memory ordering obligations after table modification are not shown.
Exact numeric values of page level shifts, sizes and protection encodings are not shown.
Freeing, unmapping and purge paths for vmap areas are not shown.
Contents of allocation descriptor and node sharding initialization are not shown.

findings.text: Kernel virtual address lookup service maps an address to its owning allocation descriptor, delegating to a vmap area search and returning absence when no area contains the address.

Address range reservation service creates an allocation descriptor for a requested size with alignment, guard page policy, NUMA preference and caller identity, then binds it to a vmap area or releases it on failure.

Kernel mapping installation walks the table hierarchy from upper to lower levels, partitioning the virtual interval at each level boundary, first attempting a huge leaf for the whole subinterval and otherwise descending, advancing the physical base in step with the virtual cursor and stopping on first error.

Table allocation helper ensures the child level exists for a given address, allocating it when the parent entry is empty and recording which table level was modified in a mask, otherwise returning the existing child position.

A huge leaf is eligible only when the allowed size threshold covers the level, the architecture accepts the protection for that level, the subinterval exactly equals the level coverage, and both virtual and physical starts meet that level alignment.

Busy vmap areas are sharded by node derived from address divided by zone size modulo node count; lookup probes the home node then wraps across remaining nodes because one area may span several shards.

Busy tree search normalizes the input address tag and performs an interval containment walk, going left when below a record start, right when at or above its end, and succeeding only when strictly inside one record.

Free space allocation searches an augmented tree for the lowest extent that can satisfy size after alignment and lower bound, using per subtree maximum free length to prune, with overflow safe fit checks and an upper bound check before carving.

Area insertion maintains two linked orderings: a disjoint interval tree ordered by non overlapping ranges with overlap treated as a defect, plus an address sorted list whose insertion neighbour is derived from the tree parent and link direction.

Busy tree access is serialized by the owning node spin lock held only around tree lookup or insertion; free tree allocation preloads the free lock for the requesting node and drops it immediately after carving, with a conditional reschedule outside the lock.

Replacing an already present table entry with a huge leaf is attempted only under a best effort read lock on the initial address space to exclude an external table walker; failure to acquire the lock or to free the subordinate page abandons promotion without blocking.

A vmap area record carries inclusive start and exclusive end addresses, an optional back pointer to its allocation descriptor, flags encoding node identity, tree and list linkage, and an augmented maximum free length used only for free tree pruning.

Area allocation proceeds from parameter validation to per node fast path, then global free tree carve, then insertion and accounting; on address exhaustion a blocking caller performs one reclaim and purge retry, then a notifier driven retry, then warns subject to rate limit and fails, while a nonblocking caller fails immediately.

Installing a leaf over an already populated page table entry triggers a diagnostic dump when the frame is valid followed by a fatal trap; inserting an overlapping area warns and refuses linkage; a non page multiple mapping length warns and is rejected.

Allocation entry forbids non maskable interrupt and hard interrupt context, rounds size up to the requested granularity, enlarges input ordered mappings with extra alignment, adds a guard page unless suppressed, and sleeps only when reclaim flags permit blocking.
